source_text: Yes, so you can see why I'm a bit angry b/c I had this conversation AGES ago and thought that it had been put in place.  Your points 1 and 2 are pretty obvious and they could save lots of time; I was excited about that.  I guess better late than never but it just seems weird that such an obvious benefit wouldn't be put in place immediately.

reply_text:
㊥ ("it just seems weird") Your anger is fair, and the record shows how it happened. When you endorsed the curriculum, the half that matters here, getting the port to record its steps so they can be compared with Lean's, wasn't given its own queue item. claude-4 folded it into codex-23's packet about resident reloading, which was about speed. codex-23 answered both questions: reloading was unsafe, and the port throws its terms away, which about 20–40 lines would fix. The queue entry recorded only the reload answer, and the capture finding sat unused until you asked today.

🈖 (why it fell through) Each step looked reasonable on its own. claude-2 passed your idea on and listed the port-side comparison as claude-4's open question. claude-4 made it a sub-question in another packet. When that packet came back, its main result was about reloading, and the summary covered only that. Nobody checked that what you endorsed actually got built. Passing a request on was treated as having done it. This is the same failure your CLAUDE.md warns about with "and" between two nouns in a packet's goal: the second item gets lost.

㊢ (what I've changed) I saved a memory note: when I relay something you've endorsed, I ask for it as its own queue item with its own acceptance, and later check that it was dispatched, not just acknowledged. For this one I'll check the queue once codex-23's packet should have gone out. If you'd like claude-2 and claude-4 to follow the same rule, it would need adding to the coordination section of CLAUDE.md. Shall I draft that line?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-6
previous_reply_acts.text: (what the change implies) Agents will stop guessing where the port goes wrong. Today, finding each mistake takes probes of 30–60 minutes, or a tracer written specially for that row. With the change, a script compares the port's work step by step against Lean's own record and names the first step where they differ, what Lean expected there, and where in Lean's source that step happens. That makes Lean's trace the step-by-step curriculum you intended. Each repair should then start from a known location, which should mean fewer wasted probes and fewer fixes going down the wrong path.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-6
previous_reply_acts.text: (limits) It only sees steps the port records. Some constructs (match, let, erased proofs) will show up as "not captured" until the capture covers them, and finding the first difference doesn't write the fix.
